title: Developer Activation & Value Props — Hosted API pricing experiments
content:
TL;DR: Shortset of developer-first value props, three quickstart angles for 15–30 minute wins, and three pricing-language experiments to test on signup flows and pricing pages. Goal: increase trial-to-API-key conversion and first-week active SDK usage for Hosted API.

Context and problem statement:
- We position Redwood Hosted API as the fast path for engineers to add LLM features without owning infra. But adoption stalls at two choke points: (1) friction during initial test (latency/cost uncertainty), (2) unclear pricing language that scares experimental usage (fear of runaway bills).
- Need messaging and microcopy that reduce perceived risk, highlight quick wins, and call out predictable economics.

Primary personas (prioritized):
- Product engineers at early-stage startups: want quick prototype, low experiment cost, simple SDK.
- Platform/ML engineers at growth companies: care about deterministic latency, metrics, and rollout controls.
- PMs evaluating integration velocity and API ergonomics.

Top-level developer-first value props (short lines for hero and sub-hero):
- Hero: "Ship LLM features fast — same API from prototype to production."
- Sub-hero bullets: "Low-friction SDKs, streaming responses, and example prompts to get results in 15 minutes." "Transparent token & request cost so experiments never surprise you." "Built-in fallback routing and deterministic latency for production readiness."

Proof points to surface where space allows:
- < 50 ms median token latency on common workloads (redwood internal benchmark) — callout on latency-sensitive doc search examples.
- Auto-batching & prefix caching reduce per-token cost by up to 3x for conversational workloads (quantified range: 1.5–3x).
- Free credits + 30-day cost protection (experiment cap) — conversation-level microbudgeting.

Quickstart angles (3 distinct 15–30 minute playbooks)
1) "Prototype in 15": minimal friction
- Steps: sign up -> copy API key -> run curl or JS SDK sample -> paste example prompt -> get streaming chat output.
- KPI we expect: first API call within 10 minutes of signup.
- Microcopy suggestions: "Paste this prompt and hit run — see results in < 1s"; CTA: "Try the sample prompt"

2) "Embed answers in your app": embeddings flow (developer comfort path)
- Steps: sample dataset upload -> run embeddings job (demo notebook) -> run similarity query in SDK sample -> render results.
- KPI: create first embedding index within first session.
- Microcopy: "Index 50 rows of your data and run a search — costs estimated up front."

3) "Ship a canary in an hour": production-like path
- Steps: use SDK + example rollout config -> set canary traffic to 5% -> view console latency/cost traces -> promote.
- KPI: canary rollout configured and metrics visible in under 60 minutes.
- Microcopy: "Test on 5% of traffic with cost guardrails and automatic fallback."

Pricing-language experiments (three variants to A/B test on signup + pricing pages)
Variant A — Transparent unit pricing (baseline)
- Headline: "Pay per token — straightforward, predictable."
- Supporting line: "Estimate cost before you run: our calculator shows token and request cost for your prompt."
- Rationale: favors technical buyers who do quick math; reduces fear of hidden metering.

Variant B — Trial-first, safety-first (risk reduction)
- Headline: "Free credits + experiment cap: try without surprises."
- Supporting line: "We’ll cap experimental spend for new projects for 30 days. Upgrade when you’re ready."
- Rationale: increases willingness to do broad experimentation. Use on landing page for product engineers.

Variant C — Outcome-oriented packaging (value framing)
- Headline: "Pay per inference — optimized for production economics."
- Supporting line: "Autoscaling, caching, and batching included — keep production costs predictable as you scale."
- Rationale: appeals to platform and growth-stage buyers who care about OPEX predictability; positions Redwood as operationally smart, not just cheap.

Microcopy snippets for flows (signup, SDK, pricing modal)
- Signup modal: "Create API key — start with $50 testing credits and automatic experiment cap."
- Billing modal: "Set monthly cap: we’ll pause API access if you hit it — no surprises."
- SDK README top-line: "npm install @redwood/inference — make your first API call in three lines."

Competitive notes (short, tactical):
- Differentiators to push: unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private (call out easy migration); clear observability (token-level cost + latency traces); cost-aware features (automatic batching, prefix cache) unique to us in hosted API messaging.
- Competitor friction to exploit: many incumbents are model-access-first, with fuzzy production guarantees and poor cost visibility. Call this out gently: "access ≠ production readiness."

Objections & quick rebuttals (sales scripting)
- "We’re worried about costs during tests." -> "Start with free credits + experiment cap; our cost estimator shows expected token spend for your prompts."
- "We need low latency and fallbacks." -> "Show the latency dashboard and our automatic regional fallback policy — it’s enabled by default for hosted customers."

Measurement plan for experiments:
- Metrics to track: time-to-first-API-call (session minutes), % of signups that run sample prompt, trial -> paid conversion at 7 and 30 days, average initial daily active API calls in first week, customer-reported surprise-billing incidents.
- Minimum detectable lift targets: +15% decrease in time-to-first-API-call, +20% in sample-prompt run rate.

Open questions / risks:
- What exact language and limits for the experiment cap? ($50 vs $100, duration 14d vs 30d).
- Do we enable experiment caps by default or opt-in during signup? Default reduces fear but may add support friction when customers want to lift caps.
- Need legal sign-off on "no surprise billing" phrasing.

Next steps / action items:
- Design: mock signup modal with Variant B copy and experiment-cap UX (owner: Priya, due: 2025-02-27).
- Eng: add simple cost estimator to sample prompt page (owner: Diego, due: 2025-03-07).
- Growth: spin up two landing page A/B tests (Variant A vs B) with sample prompt funnel tracking (owner: growth, due: 2025-03-03).

Appendix: sample hero + subcopy set for web header (single-line options)
- Option 1: "Prototype LLM features in minutes — keep production-grade economics as you scale."
- Option 2: "Start with free credits, predictable costs, and a single API from prototype to production."
- Option 3: "Developer-first LLM API: fast SDKs, transparent pricing, and built-in reliability."

Notes: keep language engineer-friendly, avoid marketing hyperbole. Tests should prioritize reducing friction over maximizing feature-listing density.
